# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

# pr-1116: feat(#1106): enable Type-2 duplication gate (crap4dart 0.11.0) + 13-file triage

## Description

Fixes #1106

## Wiring
- **Pin**: `crap4dart >=0.11.0 <0.12.0` everywhere — `packages/dap_hub/pubspec.yaml` (`^0.11.0`), ci.yml core job (line ~889), ci.yml app job (`>=0.10.0` → bounded `>=0.11.0 <0.12.0`), nightly.yml, `scripts/pre-commit` floor raised.
- **Gate**: root `crap4dart.yaml` — `duplication.enabled: true`, `severity: warning` (escalation to error stays owner-side per issue), `ignore_locals: true` (Type-2), `ignore_literals: false`, cross-module `sources: [flutter_app/lib, packages/fa_ui/lib, packages/fa_llm/lib]`. Follows the existing per-package config structure — only the root config gains the block; flutter_app/lib is covered by the cross-module scan.
- **Ratchet**: `.crap-baseline.json` (216 findings) committed. CI `Quality gates` step runs `crap4dart check --baseline`; pre-commit runs `check --staged --baseline`. Baseline count only decreases (re-save after fixes).

## CI-equivalent local proof (crap4dart 0.11.0, repo root)
```
$ dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline
[WARN] duplication: 222/829 files over 1.0% duplication
Gates: 2 passed, 1 warned, 22 skipped   (exit 0)
```
New duplication is still caught under the baseline (probe run, `--format json`): a copy of `lib/src/utils/list_equals.dart` → `lib/src/tmp_dup_probe.dart 7 50.00% duplicated lines > 1.0%`. Exit stays 0 while `severity: warning` — the issue's escalation plan flips that to failing once triage debt is paid.

## 13-file disposition
| File | Δpp | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| packages/fa_llm/lib/src/llm_config.dart | +6.8 | ignore — hand-rolled copyWith boilerplate (idiomatic Dart shape); codegen is the real fix |
| flutter_app/lib/services/home_tool.dart | +4.3 | ignore — service-tool registration closure prologue twinned across tools (structural shape, not logic) |
| lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart | +4.0 | **fixed** — `TrajectoryAssistantRecord.identityJson()` shared by export + UI cell |
| lib/src/redact/redaction_types.dart | +3.7 | ignore — hand-rolled copyWith boilerplate; codegen is the real fix |
| lib/src/approval/bash_interceptor.dart | +3.5 | **fixed** — `stripTrailingSlashes` + `globPatternMatches` migrated to shared utils |
| packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_cell.dart | +3.2 | **fixed** — cell JSON now spreads `identityJson()` |
| flutter_app/lib/services/launcher_layout_store.dart | +2.5 | **fixed** — `_tilesEqual` → foundation `listEquals` |
| flutter_app/lib/sandbox/memory_shell/awk.dart | +2.5 | ignore — argv-scan loop skeleton twinned with sandbox_builtins parseUnzipArgs; a generic scanner would obscure both |
| flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_git.dart | +2.1 | **fixed** — `_normalizeSandboxPath` → shared `normalizeLexicalPath` |
| lib/src/trajectory/search_index.dart | +2.0 | **fixed** — `_sameSources` → shared `listEquals` |
| lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart | +1.7 | **fixed** — slash prologue → `splitSlashArgs` helper |
| lib/src/cube/config/fs_policy.dart | +1.6 | **fixed** — path normalization → shared `normalizeLexicalPath` |
| lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart | +1.5 | **fixed** — trailing-slash trimming → shared `stripTrailingSlashes` |

New shared helpers: `lib/src/utils/path_text.dart` (normalizeLexicalPath, stripTrailingSlashes), `lib/src/utils/list_equals.dart` (exported via barrel), `lib/src/cli/slash_args.dart` (splitSlashArgs).

- fa_llm llm_config: **12 pass**; fa_ui trajectory details/feed/cell: **35 pass** (cell goldens show 0.19% pixel diff identically with and without this change — pre-existing host font/env drift, not from this PR)

Now I have the full diff (excluding .crap-baseline.json). Let me analyze:

1. **CI workflow changes** (ci.yml, nightly.yml): version pins bumped to `>=0.11.0 <0.12.0`. Also `check` → `check --baseline`.

2. **crap4dart.yaml**: duplication gate enabled with `severity: warning`, `ignorable: true`, `ignore_locals: true`, `ignore_literals: false`, `sources: [flutter_app/lib, packages/fa_ui/lib, packages/fa_llm/lib]`.

3. **Dart code changes**: deduplication refactors:
   - `normalizeLexicalPath` + `stripTrailingSlashes` in `lib/src/utils/path_text.dart`
   - `listEquals` in `lib/src/utils/list_equals.dart`
   - `splitSlashArgs` in `lib/src/cli/slash_args.dart`
   - `TrajectoryAssistantRecord.identityJson()` in trajectory_record.dart
   - Various callers migrated.

Now for the review, important things to check:

**Behavioral changes:**

1. `lib/src/cube/config/fs_policy.dart` `_normalize`: Old behavior — collapses `.`/`..` with `..` above root returning `null` (denied). New behavior — `_escapesRoot` pre-check then `normalizeLexicalPath`. Need to check equivalence. `_escapesRoot`: iterates segments, skipping empty and `.`; `depth += segment == '..' ? -1 : 1; if (depth < 0) return true;`. Old: `if (stack.isEmpty) return null` for `..`. Equivalent for paths that don't begin with `/`? Note: `target.split('/')` — for an absolute path `/a/b`, first segment is empty (skipped). For `..` at depth 0 → escape. Same. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

Now for the review, important things to check:

**Behavioral changes:**

1. `lib/src/cube/config/fs_policy.dart` `_normalize`: Old behavior — collapses `.`/`..` with `..` above root returning `null` (denied). New behavior — `_escapesRoot` pre-check then `normalizeLexicalPath`. Need to check equivalence. `_escapesRoot`: iterates segments, skipping empty and `.`; `depth += segment == '..' ? -1 : 1; if (depth < 0) return true;`. Old: `if (stack.isEmpty) return null` for `..`. Equivalent for paths that don't begin with `/`? Note: `target.split('/')` — for an absolute path `/a/b`, first segment is empty (skipped). For `..` at depth 0 → escape. Same. Edge case: the old `_normalize` returns `/`+stack.join — for empty stack returns `/`. New: `normalizeLexicalPath` returns `'/' + segments.join('/')` = `/` for empty. Equivalent.

   Wait, one subtle difference: `_escapesRoot` counts depth with non-empty non-`.` segments. But `normalizeLexicalPath` clamps `..` when segments is empty. The pre-check denies escapes before normalizing, so behavior preserved. OK.

Read input context:

callers/callees of changed symbols,

Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. # crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

# Bootstrap (2026-09-15): 2450.0 — `JsAppEngine._faCall` (CC 49, 0% line
# coverage). Descent #1 (same day): the issue's three named offenders went
# under the next milestone line (CRAP ≤ 40 each) and the threshold followed
# the measured new worst: 2450.0 → 870.0 (`wasm_shell_git.run` and
# `main`, CC 29 at 0% coverage). Descent #2 (issue #475): both beasts
# decomposed into route-table dispatch + per-family handlers with a 51-test
# golden suite, and the cluster's own 812/702/600/506 beasts went down with
# them; the threshold follows the new measured worst: 870.0 → 650.0
# (`runCodemieSsoFlow`, CC 25 at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card).
# Descent #9 (issue #485): the on-device provider stream functions moved to
# one shared pump + codec walk (lib/on_device/), and the beasts went down
# with them — gemma 992 → 9, transformers.js 552/506 → 17/1, webllm 420 → 6
# (all fully covered by the provider suites + the new codec-table/pump
# tests); the threshold follows the measured new worst: 650.0 → 380.0
# (`WasiSandboxShell._runStage`, CC 19 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell cluster,
# another lane's ladder card).
# Pushes may only make the codebase BETTER,
# never worse; scripts/check_crap_guards.py --only-down rejects a raised
# threshold in CI. The staged ladder continues in follow-up cards:
# 870 → … → 40 (see AGENTS.md "Quality gates"). Re-measure after each fix:
# cd flutter_app && flutter test --coverage &&
# dart pub global run crap4dart analyze.

sources: [lib]

# Same generated set as the root config (E1 parity — asserted by
# scripts/check_crap_guards.py).
exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in flutter_app/lib under the flutter lcov
  # pipeline. Descent #10 (issue #558): the wasm_shell pipeline-engine
  # cluster went down (_runStage 380→4, _runPipeline 210→4, _evalExpr
  # 182→3, _rewriteRelativeArgs 110→2, _maybeRewritePath 72→3, all 100%
  # covered by test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows
  # the measured new worst: 380.0 → 272.0 (`WasiSandboxShell._xargsBuiltin`,
  # CC 16 at 0% cov — the wasm_shell builtins cluster, the next lane's
  # ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #11 (issue #559): the wasm_shell builtins cluster went down

  # driven parse helpers now live in wasm_shell_builtins.dart with direct
  # unit tests, the exec halves are covered e2e in
  # test/wasm_shell_pipeline_test.dart); the threshold follows the
  # measured new worst: 272.0 → 210.0 (`GemmaService.chatStream`, CC 14
  # at 0% cov — another lane's ladder card). Only down.
  # Descent #12 (issue #701): the 0%-coverage trio went down (_statBuiltin
  # 156→12.1 @ 91% cov via test/wasm_shell_stat_test.dart, isFaCliInstalled
  # 110→6 via the extracted faCliProbe seam + test/sessions_root_test.dart,
  # _showAppMenu 90→9 @ 100% cov via test/apps/apps_panel_menu_test.dart);
  # the threshold follows the measured new worst: 210.0 → 30.0 (the CC-5
  # 0%-cov tier: routeExtHostMessage, codemie _createController, attached
  # _AttachedRow.build, GemmaService.loadModel — the next ladder cards).
  # Re-measured on the CI pipeline (app-crap-gate run 35479048998): local
  # lcov is impossible on the agent cube (the flutter coverage collector
  # canonicalizes source paths and lstat EPERMs through .worktrees). Only
  # down.
  # TEMP raise (owner call 2026-09-26, mirrors dmtools-dart #256): the #955
  # network-mode merge shipped widgets without tests — max CRAP 72.0
  # (_ChannelRailState._createChannel, CC 8 @ 0% cov). Restore to 30.0 via
  # the linked issue.
  # raise-issue: gh-992
  # Restored (gh-992, 2026-09-27): the agents/enroll DAP-tab rework
  # (fcd2d0232) covered the #955 network UI — 5 enroll dialog groups +
  # channel_rail/chat_page call-site suites, 72 focused tests; re-measured
  # on the full local flutter lcov (3292 green): max CRAP 30.0, the
  # threshold follows back down 75.0 → 30.0. Only down.
  threshold: 30.0

coverage:
  # The CI app-crap-gate job merges the two flutter-tests shard reports
  # (scripts/merge_lcov.py) right before the CRAP step. Pre-commit stays
  # core-only: flutter coverage is too heavy for every commit.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  # flutter's lcov carries no BRDA branch records; branch coverage stays
  # a core-package gate concern.
  branch_coverage: false
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole flutter suite
  # first. Coverage comes from the CI shard merge (scripts/merge_lcov.py)
  # and pre-commit stays core-only (#433 split); nobody wants a second
  # suite run inside a 6-minute gate job.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# This config is the single source of which gates `crap4dart check` runs
# (CI app-crap-gate job, pre-commit core hook): 0.9.5 default-enables ALL
# built-in gates, so everything not enforced below is disabled explicitly.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)

  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over the golden set (165 PNGs). severity: warning + the

  # broke the 40 pre-font goldens of de2f11b9 (solid Ahem text
  # rectangles, hollow icon squares without an X) and false-positives on:
  #   - the Habit Tracker checkmark tile (green square + white V
  #     converging like an X signature; light theme only, the same 22px
  #     tile at x=234 in all 5 hits),

  # `severity: error` and drop the excludes when the upstream detector
  # fixes land — scripts/check_golden_detector.py re-verifies all six
  # classes against this exact detector (see its docstring).
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test/golden/goldens]
    exclude:
      # false positives: green checkmark tile reads as an X (light theme)
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/grid_light.png'
      - 'test/golden/goldens/launcher/sheet_bar_light.png'

  # Widget → golden coverage. WARNING (not error): the 0.9.5 widget

1. The flutter_app `crap4dart.yaml` has `duplication: {enabled: false}` with a comment "own jscpd <1% guard (global %) — 0.10.0's `duplication.sources` cross-module key stays available...". The root config now enables duplication with cross-module sources. The PR description says: "Follows the existing per-package config structure — only the root config gains the block; flutter_app/lib is covered by the cross-module scan."

   But wait — the CI flutter_app job (`app-crap-gate`) runs `cd flutter_app && dart pub global run crap4dart analyze` with flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml which has duplication disabled. So the cross-module duplication gate only runs in the core job's analyze + check --baseline (both from repo root). That's what the PR description says — consistent.

2. `scripts/check_crap_guards.py` — checks README badge == config threshold, generated-exclude parity between the two configs, and --only-down. The duplication block in root config — does the parity check compare whole gates sections? Let me read check_crap_guards.py fully to be sure the new duplication block doesn't break "generated-exclude parity" (it compares `exclude:` lists presumably). The exclude lists are unchanged. Probably fine. Let me quickly scan it.

3. `ignorable: true` — the `// crap:ignore` comments are in flutter_app files (home_tool.dart, awk.dart) and fa_ui/fa_llm files. When CI flutter_app job runs `crap4dart analyze` from flutter_app/, duplication is disabled there so ignores don't matter. When the core root scan runs with cross-module sources, `ignorable: true` applies. But do ignore comments require `ignorable: true` per the scanning config — yes. OK.

   One question: does the pre-commit `check --staged --baseline` respect ignores? Should.

"cross-module scope from #487" — presumably the duplication gate scans the union of root sources [lib, bin] + gate sources? Or only the listed three? If `sources` replaces the scope for the duplication gate, then lib/ and bin/ wouldn't be scanned for duplication... but the baseline contains findings in `bin/` and `lib/` files (bin/fah_hub_plugin.dart 6.15%, etc.) and flutter_app/lib — the baseline says "222/829 files over 1.0%". So the scan covers everything — root sources + gate sources union. OK, consistent.

Minor doc nit — the flutter_app config comment says "mirrors the root crap4dart.yaml" which no longer mirrors (root now has duplication ENABLED, flutter_app still disabled with a comment describing the old state). Actually wait — is that a problem? The flutter_app config retains `duplication: {enabled: false}` — meaning when CI app job runs `check`/`analyze` for the app, no duplication gate. The PR description says this is intentional (cross-module scan from root covers flutter_app/lib). Hmm, but does the root scan actually run for app-only PRs? CI core job condition: `needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'`. If a PR only touches flutter_app files, does the core "Quality gates" step run? Let me check the ci.yml conditions for the Quality gates step: `if: needs.changes.outputs.core == 'true' || needs.changes.outputs.shared == 'true'`. And the duplication analyze step has the same condition. So for app-only PRs, the cross-module duplication gate does NOT run in CI... but the `guards` job runs `check_dup_cross_module.sh` "which also runs it for app-only PRs". The jscpd guards still cover app-only PRs (global % thresholds). The new Type-2 gate from root only runs on core/shared PRs. So app-only duplication regressions that pass the jscpd <3.7% global guard wouldn't be caught by the new gate — acceptable per PR description ("flutter_app/lib is covered by the cross-module scan") but that's only true for core/shared-triggered runs. Minor gap; arguably a SUGGESTION.

Plus the root `sources: [lib, bin]` presumably also scanned by the duplication gate. The baseline includes bin/ and lib/ findings — confirming lib/bin are scanned.

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,

callers/callees of changed symbols,

Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. - **Title**: feat(#1106): enable Type-2 duplication gate (crap4dart 0.11.0) + 13-file triage
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit

- **State**: open

- **Additions**: +1505
- **Deletions**: -215
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T15:36:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T15:54:10Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1106

## Wiring
- **Pin**: `crap4dart >=0.11.0 <0.12.0` everywhere — `packages/dap_hub/pubspec.yaml` (`^0.11.0`), ci.yml core job (line ~889), ci.yml app job (`>=0.10.0` → bounded `>=0.11.0 <0.12.0`), nightly.yml, `scripts/pre-commit` floor raised.
- **Gate**: root `crap4dart.yaml` — `duplication.enabled: true`, `severity: warning` (escalation to error stays owner-side per issue), `ignore_locals: true` (Type-2), `ignore_literals: false`, cross-module `sources: [flutter_app/lib, packages/fa_ui/lib, packages/fa_llm/lib]`. Follows the existing per-package config structure — only the root config gains the block; flutter_app/lib is covered by the cross-module scan.
- **Ratchet**: `.crap-baseline.json` (216 findings) committed. CI `Quality gates` step runs `crap4dart check --baseline`; pre-commit runs `check --staged --baseline`. Baseline count only decreases (re-save after fixes).

## CI-equivalent local proof (crap4dart 0.11.0, repo root)
```
$ dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline
[WARN] duplication: 222/829 files over 1.0% duplication
Gates: 2 passed, 1 warned, 22 skipped   (exit 0)
```
New duplication is still caught under the baseline (probe run, `--format json`): a copy of `lib/src/utils/list_equals.dart` → `lib/src/tmp_dup_probe.dart 7 50.00% duplicated lines > 1.0%`. Exit stays 0 while `severity: warning` — the issue's escalation plan flips that to failing once triage debt is paid.

## 13-file disposition
| File | Δpp | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| packages/fa_llm/lib/src/llm_config.dart | +6.8 | ignore — hand-rolled copyWith boilerplate (idiomatic Dart shape); codegen is the real fix |
| flutter_app/lib/services/home_tool.dart | +4.3 | ignore — service-tool registration closure prologue twinned across tools (structural shape, not logic) |
| lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart | +4.0 | **fixed** — `TrajectoryAssistantRecord.identityJson()` shared by export + UI cell |
| lib/src/redact/redaction_types.dart | +3.7 | ignore — hand-rolled copyWith boilerplate; codegen is the real fix |
| lib/src/approval/bash_interceptor.dart | +3.5 | **fixed** — `stripTrailingSlashes` + `globPatternMatches` migrated to shared utils |
| packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_cell.dart | +3.2 | **fixed** — cell JSON now spreads `identityJson()` |
| flutter_app/lib/services/launcher_layout_store.dart | +2.5 | **fixed** — `_tilesEqual` → foundation `listEquals` |
| flutter_app/lib/sandbox/memory_shell/awk.dart | +2.5 | ignore — argv-scan loop skeleton twinned with sandbox_builtins parseUnzipArgs; a generic scanner would obscure both |
| flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_git.dart | +2.1 | **fixed** — `_normalizeSandboxPath` → shared `normalizeLexicalPath` |
| lib/src/trajectory/search_index.dart | +2.0 | **fixed** — `_sameSources` → shared `listEquals` |
| lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart | +1.7 | **fixed** — slash prologue → `splitSlashArgs` helper |
| lib/src/cube/config/fs_policy.dart | +1.6 | **fixed** — path normalization → shared `normalizeLexicalPath` |
| lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart | +1.5 | **fixed** — trailing-slash trimming → shared `stripTrailingSlashes` |

New shared helpers: `lib/src/utils/path_text.dart` (normalizeLexicalPath, stripTrailingSlashes), `lib/src/utils/list_equals.dart` (exported via barrel), `lib/src/cli/slash_args.dart` (splitSlashArgs).

## Verification
- core `dart test` (types, redact config, roles_config, fs_policy, extension_host, fuzzy_matcher, search_index, trajectory_export, bash_interceptor): **256 pass**; agent_cli (slash paths): **89 pass**
- fa_llm llm_config: **12 pass**; fa_ui trajectory details/feed/cell: **35 pass** (cell goldens show 0.19% pixel diff identically with and without this change — pre-existing host font/env drift, not from this PR)
- flutter_app (home_tool, launcher_layout_store, app_launcher_screen, memory_shell ×2, sandbox_ssh, wasm_shell_builtins, web_git ×2): **370 pass**
- `dart analyze` core+fa_llm: clean on all touched files; `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in touched files (103 infos = pre-existing baseline)

## Remaining debt (owner-side escalation follow-up)
- 216 baseline findings (6 justified ignores pinned in code; the rest are the standing Type-1/Type-2 tail below the per-file 1% bar or outside the 13-file worklist)
- flip `severity: warning` → `error` once the debt is paid

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and

  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]

      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score

blocks.text:
# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review"] O2["Write outputs/pr_review_general.md — brief general PR comment (1-2 paragraphs max)"] O3["Write ou…

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1116
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1116
- **Title**: feat(#1106): enable Type-2 duplication gate (crap4dart 0.11.0) + 13-file triage
- **Author**: vabhzw17eg2qu4m9-bit
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1106` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 34
- **Additions**: +1505
- **Deletions**: -215
- **Created**: 2026-09-30T15:36:39Z
- **Updated**: 2026-09-30T15:54:10Z

## PR Description

Fixes #1106

## Wiring
- **Pin**: `crap4dart >=0.11.0 <0.12.0` everywhere — `packages/dap_hub/pubspec.yaml` (`^0.11.0`), ci.yml core job (line ~889), ci.yml app job (`>=0.10.0` → bounded `>=0.11.0 <0.12.0`), nightly.yml, `scripts/pre-commit` floor raised.
- **Gate**: root `crap4dart.yaml` — `duplication.enabled: true`, `severity: warning` (escalation to error stays owner-side per issue), `ignore_locals: true` (Type-2), `ignore_literals: false`, cross-module `sources: [flutter_app/lib, packages/fa_ui/lib, packages/fa_llm/lib]`. Follows the existing per-package config structure — only the root config gains the block; flutter_app/lib is covered by the cross-module scan.
- **Ratchet**: `.crap-baseline.json` (216 findings) committed. CI `Quality gates` step runs `crap4dart check --baseline`; pre-commit runs `check --staged --baseline`. Baseline count only decreases (re-save after fixes).

## CI-equivalent local proof (crap4dart 0.11.0, repo root)
```
$ dart pub global run crap4dart check --baseline
[WARN] duplication: 222/829 files over 1.0% duplication
Gates: 2 passed, 1 warned, 22 skipped   (exit 0)
```
New duplication is still caught under the baseline (probe run, `--format json`): a copy of `lib/src/utils/list_equals.dart` → `lib/src/tmp_dup_probe.dart 7 50.00% duplicated lines > 1.0%`. Exit stays 0 while `severity: warning` — the issue's escalation plan flips that to failing once triage debt is paid.

## 13-file disposition
| File | Δpp | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| packages/fa_llm/lib/src/llm_config.dart | +6.8 | ignore — hand-rolled copyWith boilerplate (idiomatic Dart shape); codegen is the real fix |
| flutter_app/lib/services/home_tool.dart | +4.3 | ignore — service-tool registration closure prologue twinned across tools (structural shape, not logic) |
| lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_export.dart | +4.0 | **fixed** — `TrajectoryAssistantRecord.identityJson()` shared by export + UI cell |
| lib/src/redact/redaction_types.dart | +3.7 | ignore — hand-rolled copyWith boilerplate; codegen is the real fix |
| lib/src/approval/bash_interceptor.dart | +3.5 | **fixed** — `stripTrailingSlashes` + `globPatternMatches` migrated to shared utils |
| packages/fa_ui/lib/src/trajectory/trajectory_cell.dart | +3.2 | **fixed** — cell JSON now spreads `identityJson()` |
| flutter_app/lib/services/launcher_layout_store.dart | +2.5 | **fixed** — `_tilesEqual` → foundation `listEquals` |
| flutter_app/lib/sandbox/memory_shell/awk.dart | +2.5 | ignore — argv-scan loop skeleton twinned with sandbox_builtins parseUnzipArgs; a generic scanner would obscure both |
| flutter_app/lib/sandbox/web_git.dart | +2.1 | **fixed** — `_normalizeSandboxPath` → shared `normalizeLexicalPath` |
| lib/src/trajectory/search_index.dart | +2.0 | **fixed** — `_sameSources` → shared `listEquals` |
| lib/src/cli/skill_commands.dart | +1.7 | **fixed** — slash prologue → `splitSlashArgs` helper |
| lib/src/cube/config/fs_policy.dart | +1.6 | **fixed** — path normalization → shared `normalizeLexicalPath` |
| lib/src/model_roles/roles_config.dart | +1.5 | **fixed** — trailing-slash trimming → shared `stripTrailingSlashes` |

New shared helpers: `lib/src/utils/path_text.dart` (normalizeLexicalPath, stripTrailingSlashes), `lib/src/utils/list_equals.dart` (exported via barrel), `lib/src/cli/slash_args.dart` (splitSlashArgs).

## Verification
- core `dart test` (types, redact config, roles_config, fs_policy, extension_host, fuzzy_matcher, search_index, trajectory_export, bash_interceptor): **256 pass**; agent_cli (slash paths): **89 pass**
- fa_llm llm_config: **12 pass**; fa_ui trajectory details/feed/cell: **35 pass** (cell goldens show 0.19% pixel diff identically with and without this change — pre-existing host font/env drift, not from this PR)
- flutter_app (home_tool, launcher_layout_store, app_launcher_screen, memory_shell ×2, sandbox_ssh, wasm_shell_builtins, web_git ×2): **370 pass**
- `dart analyze` core+fa_llm: clean on all touched files; `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos --no-fatal-warnings`: no issues in touched files (103 infos = pre-existing baseline)

## Remaining debt (owner-side escalation follow-up)
- 216 baseline findings (6 justified ignores pinned in code; the rest are the standing Type-1/Type-2 tail below the per-file 1% bar or outside the 13-file worklist)
- flip `severity: warning` → `error` once the debt is paid

# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_rep…

blocks.text:
# crap4dart configuration for flutter_agent_harness.
# https://github.com/IstiN/crap4dart
#
# RATCHET: the CRAP threshold is pinned at the current worst score
# (356.34, `_handleKey` in bin/../tui_repl.dart) — pushes may only make
# the codebase BETTER, never worse. Lower the threshold whenever the top
# offenders are fixed (run: dart pub global run crap4dart analyze).

sources: [lib, bin]

exclude:
  - '**.g.dart'
  - '**.freezed.dart'
  - '**.mocks.dart'
  - 'build/**'
  - 'vendor/**'

crap:
  enabled: true
  # Current max CRAP score in the repo (2026-08-12 — GREEN zone after the
  # cleanup rounds 356.34 → 65.1 → 16 → 8 → 12; three TUI-only dispatchers
  # at CC 3 / 0% cov land at CRAP 12 — they need a real PTY to test). Only
  # down from here.
  threshold: 12.0
# NOTE: _listModels (provider_commands.dart) hits 20 with 0% coverage
# because it is line-mode-only output; it pre-dates the dial work. Fix
# separately — do not ratchet up for it.

coverage:
  # scripts/pre-commit regenerates this (dart test --coverage) right
  # before the CRAP step runs.
  lcov_path: coverage/lcov.info
  required: true
  branch_coverage: true
  # crap4dart 0.9.5 flipped the run_tests default to true — a bare
  # `analyze`/`check` would silently re-run the whole core suite first.
  # Coverage is regenerated explicitly (pre-commit hook, CI shard merge);
  # do not pay for it twice.
  run_tests: false

# ─── Gates (issue #447) ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# 0.9.5 default-enables ALL built-in gates; only broken_goldens is
# enforced here, everything else is disabled explicitly so a bare
# `check --staged` (pre-commit, core-only #433 split) means exactly the
# pixel gate. The flutter_app goldens live in flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml.
gates:
  loc: {enabled: false} # own ≤2800 gate (scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh)
  test_coverage: {enabled: false} # own ≥80% coverage-gate job
  complexity: {enabled: false} # CRAP ratchet above already covers it
  method_size: {enabled: false}
  nesting: {enabled: false}
  class_size: {enabled: false}
  weight_of_class: {enabled: false}
  unused_code: {enabled: false}
  unused_files: {enabled: false}
  banned_imports: {enabled: false}
  # Type-2 duplication gate (issue #1106, crap4dart 0.11.0). Renamed-clone
  # detection on top of the Type-1 default; the union with the raw pass can
  # only ADD findings, never lose exact copies. severity: warning starts
  # soft — escalate to error once the 13-file triage debt is paid
  # (follow-up, owner-side). The global jscpd <1% guards stay as-is.
  duplication:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    ignorable: true # enables `// crap:ignore` for justified structural twins
    ignore_locals: true # Type-2: rename locals before hashing (API names stay)
    ignore_literals: false # keeps l10n/theme/symbol tables out
    sources: # cross-module scope from #487
      - flutter_app/lib
      - packages/fa_ui/lib
      - packages/fa_llm/lib
  file_naming: {enabled: false}
  magic_constants: {enabled: false}
  test_assertions: {enabled: false}
  folder_structure: {enabled: false}
  external: {enabled: false}
  public_docs: {enabled: false}
  golden: {enabled: false} # flutter-only gate (core is not a Flutter project)
  accessibility: {enabled: false}
  hardcoded_strings: {enabled: false}

  # Pixel gate over core test/ goldens — none exist today, so this is a
  # no-op that guards the future (issue #447 AC: "and core test/ goldens
  # if any appear"). WARNING, same rationale as flutter_app: the 0.9.5
  # detector misses the Ahem-solid-rect and hollow-square classes and
  # false-positives on V-converging shapes; flip to error when the
  # upstream detector fixes land.
  broken_goldens:
    enabled: true
    severity: warning
    dirs: [test]
    exclude:
      # TUI screenshots, not goldens: amber/yellow text on the dark theme
      # trips the stripe heuristic (measured 14/14 "overflow stripes" —
      # the same yellow-on-dark detector bug the issue documents for
      # apps_panel/panel_dark). Revisit when upstream fixes land.
      - 'test/integration/**'

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. New shared helpers: `lib/src/utils/path_text.dart` (normalizeLexicalPath, stripTrailingSlashes), `lib/src/utils/list_equals.dart` (exported via barrel), `lib/src/cli/slash_args.dart` (splitSlashArgs).

- flip `severity: warning` → `error` once the debt is paid

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

Issue #177 restructured CI so a PR pays only for what it touched. The hook
is a thin wrapper over `scripts/ci_fast_gate.sh`; CI is NOT the same
process — it implements the same stages as parallel jobs, and since
issue #194 its PR path classification runs through the SAME script
(`ci_fast_gate.sh --dry-run` in the `changes` job). One classifier, one
set of thresholds; parity is checkable by diffing the hook's
`GATE_STAGE <name> OK|SKIP` markers against the stages the CI changes job
logs for the same diff. Path filters: docs/markdown/prompts-only →
size+analyze; lib/bin/test/example/pubspec → +tests, coverage, CRAP,
jscpd + cross-module dupx; `test/integration/**` → + `integration-mock`
(issue #551: the no-key legs run per-PR); flutter_app/packages → +dupx,
flutter analyze+tests;
scripts/.github/crap4dart.yaml/unknown → everything (safe default, E2 —
holds in CI too). Hook-only extras: dart format self-heal of staged files
and `scripts/check_goldens.py --quick` (skipped for docs-only commits).

- `dart analyze` + dart format clean (explicit dirs — `yoclip/` is a
  standalone video workspace with its own toolchain); example app also
